query_budget: Follow-up retrieval of one named source
existing_reused_note: No stored record describes CCGA, GRAIL or these classifiers, so every method, configuration and dataset is new. No metric block is shared with another batch and no vocabulary concept was added: the batch reuses sensitivity-at-98-percent-specificity and accuracy.
sample_overlap_note: None. The CCGA sequencing data are not public (Data and code availability). The cohorts behind the existing judgements are cfMethyl-Seq (EGAD00001009003 and the 408-sample cfMethyl-Seq cohort), EGAD00001000856 liver WGBS, in silico mixtures, the SPOT-MAS Vietnam cohorts, DELFI 2019, Jiang et al. 2018, Mathios et al. 2021, Zhou et al. 2022 and the pooled UNITE set; none draws on CCGA. The three protocols here share one set of CCGA participants with each other.

limitations: Developer study: GRAIL designed the assays and classifiers, ran every arm, and reports the comparison.

Case-control enrolment of clinically diagnosed cancers and matched non-cancer participants, not an intended-use screening population.

relevance_note: Methylation: the training and validation detection protocols are direct, because they measure the use case's declared endpoint (all-stage sensitivity at a declared specificity on plasma cfDNA), as the stored cfMethyl-Seq judgement does; the post hoc threshold, case-control design and developer origin are limitations, not a change of endpoint. Tissue of origin is proxy, as the stored SPOT-MAS judgements are. Fragmentomics: both detection protocols are proxy, consistent with the reviewed fragmentomics judgements, because the use case asks for performance under low tumour fractions and no stratified sensitivity is printed.

use_case_changes.note: Proposed for the integrator; neither use_case record was edited.

evidence_gaps_replace.No sensitivity at a declared specificity: The only same-sample comparison at a declared specificity (Jamshidi et al. 2022) is developer-run on prototype assays, with the 98% specificity threshold set post hoc within each set.

evidence_gaps_add: Jamshidi et al. 2022 tissue-of-origin accuracy is scored on 127 cancers detected by all three classifiers and counts 'other' as correct for six cancer types; the Results and Methods name different classifier triples for that set.
use-case-plasma-ctdna-methylation.exclusion_change_proposed: The second exclusion says the only tissue-of-origin comparison uses combined features. Jamshidi et al. 2022 adds a methylation-only origin classifier compared with two non-methylation classifiers on the same cancers, so the reviewer may want to narrow it, for example: 'Tissue-of-origin identification outside detected cancers: the tissue-of-origin results ingested classify cancer patients only.'
use-case-plasma-ctdna-methylation.summary_addition_proposed: Jamshidi et al. 2022 (Cancer Cell), the GRAIL developers, compared ten prototype classifiers on the same CCGA substudy 1 participants at a 98% specificity threshold set post hoc within each set. On the independent validation set (464 cancers, 362 non-cancers), the whole-genome bisulfite methylation classifier detected 34% (95% CI 30%-39%; 158 of 464), against 33% for variants with white-blood-cell correction, 30% for copy number with white-blood-cell correction, 29% for fragment lengths, 27% for copy number, 22% for allelic imbalance, 18% for fragment endpoints and 16% for uncorrected variants; a classifier over all scores reached 36%. Among 127 validation cancers detected by all three representative classifiers, the methylation origin classifier assigned the correct tissue in 75% (95 of 127), against 41% for copy number and 35% for corrected variants. These are case-control results from the assay developer, not screening performance, and the targeted methylation test GRAIL developed afterwards is a different assay.

evidence_gaps_add: Jamshidi et al. 2022 fragment classifiers were developed after validation blinding was lifted, and their clinical limits of detection by tumour allele fraction are in figures only.
use-case-plasma-ctdna-fragmentomics.summary_addition_proposed: Jamshidi et al. 2022 (Cancer Cell), the GRAIL developers, also scored two fragmentomic classifiers from 30x cfDNA whole-genome sequencing on the same CCGA substudy 1 participants as their methylation, copy-number and variant classifiers, at a 98% specificity threshold set post hoc within each set. On the independent validation set (464 cancers, 362 non-cancers), the fragment length classifier detected 29% (95% CI 25%-34%) and the fragment endpoint classifier 18% (15%-22%), against 34% for whole-genome methylation; both fragment classifiers were developed after validation blinding was lifted, and no tumour-fraction-stratified sensitivity is printed.
